George Willard walked slowly down Main Street, hands in his pockets, noticing for the first time how small the town was. The lamps were being lit; a farmer’s wagon creaked past, loaded with sacks. In the window of the hardware store an old man sat reading a newspaper, and George wondered what lay behind that sagging, patient face. Every person in Winesburg, he thought, seemed to carry a secret like a stone in a pocket — something that they turned over and over, and never showed. He had listened to many of them, and had written nothing down. At the end of the street he paused, uncertain, and looked toward the station where the evening train was due.
